runtime.execution: Async get_asv agent/environment loop, operation graph with call IDs, concurrent rollouts and prompt/memory optimizers.

summary: Explicit state transitions and trainable operation programs support agent-policy experiments; graph/state capture is narrower than complete original audit.

inspection.scope: Read Simple/ReAct state and get_asv, rollout step/callback/error/timing, OpResult/OpCtx, LLM call capture, APE prompt update, HTTP agent client and window/optimizer tests.
inspection.limits: Not full memory/tree/local-weights agent variants; alleged DB rehydration comments are not verified implemented persistence; no providers or evaluation executed.

complaints.detail: complaints: this reference supplies trainable agent computation-graph and rollout framework; an agent policy, model interface and context lifecycle are outside its supplied role.

authority.detail: Registered environment owns tools; caller programs/optimizer can mutate prompts; generic operator approval/agency posture is application work.

evaluation.detail: Trajectory reward/gradient supplies feedback; window test checks protocol pairing, optimizer tests observe prompt trace/reset and task loss.

time_order.detail: Monotonic per-operation timings plus trajectory timestep and call IDs; no restart/paused-time policy.

evidence.claim: Next-state creation can window transitions, hide prior environment state and hide action content without mutating prior state.
get_asv gets next state, resolves config/model op and appends chosen action.
Rollout explicitly calls agent then environment, stores before/after state/action/reward/done/truncated and timer metadata.
Op context stores run/call keyed data globally, excluded from model_dump and clearable; DB rehydration discussed but not implemented by these methods.
LLM call uses supplied model-chain configuration; result/logprob saved in Op context, returns first message.
Optimizer selects trajectory examples and updates prompt under lock; template-variable check is gate, not held-out improvement test.
HTTP client passes serialized state/observations/training mode and receives action/next state/value.
Monotonic operation duration and semaphore limit bound rollout concurrency.
Sliding window test expects exact user/hidden/tool-request/tool-response sequence after five transitions.

tests.focus: Window transformation retains valid tool request/response transition.
tests.oracle: Exactly four expected messages with user/hidden/request/response types; provider calls use test fixtures/cassettes, no raw original-audit assertion.

tests.focus: APE example aggregation, update reset and learned task loss.
tests.oracle: Known good examples, empty consumed example set and growing prompt trace; task-specific loss improvement with retries, not universal harness invariants.

strengths: Ordinary explicit agent/environment states make research and alternative policy paradigms composable.
Operations carry call identities and trainable parameters; state/trace are separable from model messages.
limits: A useful graph trace is not an immutable original audit; comments about DB persistence require separate implementation evidence.
Template-compatible prompt updates are not independent improvement evidence or safe native core refit.
arconaut_questions: How should active context, retained original state and learned policy parameters have separate identities/lifetimes?
Can the model experiment with decision programs while independent correctness oracles remain outside editable policy?
